children: PTC Industries has issued a qualified institutional placement (QIP) of up to Rs 1,800 crore, with the company looking to use the bulk of the proceeds to reduce debt and strengthen its balance sheet following a sharp improvement in quarterly earnings.

The fundraise will result in equity dilution of around 5.7 per cent of the company’s pre-issue paid-up equity capital. PTC Industries has set an indicative floor price of Rs 21,060 per share, representing an 8.9 per cent discount to its previous closing price.

Debt repayment is the primary use of the proceeds, which could lower the company’s finance costs and improve its balance-sheet position. A portion of the capital will be deployed into subsidiary Aerolloy Technologies for working capital and machinery purchases.
The fundraise comes after a strong first quarter for PTC Industries, with revenue and profitability rising sharply from a year earlier.
Consolidated profit after tax attributable to owners rose more than five-fold to Rs 29.19 crore in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, compared with Rs 5.16 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Revenue from operations increased 97.4 per cent year-on-year to Rs 191.80 crore from Rs 97.15 crore. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) climbed nearly 180 per cent to Rs 54.21 crore from Rs 19.35 crore.
The stronger operating performance came despite a 62.55 per cent increase in consolidated expenses, which stood at Rs 160.37 crore in the June quarter against Rs 98.66 crore a year earlier.

The QIP will therefore bring fresh institutional capital into the company after a period of strong earnings growth, while the proposed debt reduction is expected to provide some relief on the financing side and support further investment in Aerolloy Technologies.
